prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: After loading a persisted OAuthToken from storage, OAuthContext never restores token_expiry_time (it's only set at the moment a token is freshly issued/refreshed). This makes is_token_valid() treat a stale/expired cached token as still valid across a process restart, so proactive refresh never triggers and the client either sends an expired token or falls through to a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: After loading a persisted OAuthToken from storage, OAuthContext never restores token_expiry_time (it's only set at the moment a token is freshly issued/refreshed). This makes is_token_valid() treat a stale/expired cached token as still valid across a process restart, so proactive refresh never triggers and the client either sends an expired token or falls through to a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs trace back to the same gap: _initialize() doesn't recompute token_expiry_time when it loads a stored OAuthToken. #1784 fixes this at the source with a 4-line change in _initialize() (calling context.update_token_expiry when expires_in is present) plus a dedicated expired_tokens fixture/test. #2875's own inline comment states the identical root cause ('A provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time, so is_token_valid() treats the stale token as valid... the proactive-refresh branch above is skipped') but instead of restoring the field, it adds a larger workaround inside the 401-handling branch of async_auth_flow that tries the stored refresh_token before falling back to full re-authorization. That workaround only runs after a request has already failed with an expired token, whereas fixing _initialize() directly restores proactive refresh and prevents the unnecessary failed request in the first place, making #2875's added branch redundant once applied.

prs.author: Bartok9

prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2962's fix is grounded in a specific spec citation (SEP-1577) and a linked issue (#2960) demonstrating that raising here is a spec-compliance bug, not just a bad message — a tool_use is not required to be followed by a tool_result. #3053's diff assumes the opposite: that raising in this case is correct and only the wording needs improving, which reintroduces the exact false-positive #2962 fixes. prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add a quote/escape-aware comma splitter for WWW-Authenticate in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py, but #3012's diff is the more complete and minimal fix: it deletes the now-dead `import re`, showing the old regex-based substring matcher is fully replaced by a single `_iter_www_auth_params` helper feeding directly into `extract_field_from_www_auth`. #3041 instead introduces two cooperating helpers (`_split_www_authenticate_segments` + `_extract_bearer_auth_params`) that add roughly double the net new lines (~82 vs ~39) for the same fix, and its Bearer-scheme-detection loop is cut off before completing its stop condition in the diff, making its full correctness harder to verify. #3012 also keeps the change scoped to fixing the exact substring-match bug without adding scheme-disambiguation logic that isn't exercised by the single-challenge case this codebase actually handles.

prs.title: fix(client/auth): discover AS metadata before cold-start token refresh, with issuer-binding check
prs.author: app/claude
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuthContext.oauth_metadata (the discovered authorization-server metadata, including the token endpoint) only lives in memory and is never available on a fresh process start. When a client is reloaded from storage with a stored refresh_token but no in-memory oauth_metadata, the refresh flow has no way to find the correct token endpoint, breaking silent token refresh after a restart ('cold start'). (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuthContext.oauth_metadata (the discovered authorization-server metadata, including the token endpoint) only lives in memory and is never available on a fresh process start. When a client is reloaded from storage with a stored refresh_token but no in-memory oauth_metadata, the refresh flow has no way to find the correct token endpoint, breaking silent token refresh after a restart ('cold start'). (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs target the missing oauth_metadata on cold start, but via different mechanisms. #2492 adds get_oauth_metadata/set_oauth_metadata to the TokenStorage protocol and persists metadata externally, but the new methods default to no-ops in the base class, so the refresh-after-restart bug remains unfixed for any existing TokenStorage implementation that isn't updated to actually persist metadata. #3263 fixes the same gap unconditionally on the client side by re-running AS discovery before a cold-start refresh whenever oauth_metadata is missing, and additionally adds an issuer-binding check plus an eager_discovery_attempted flag to avoid re-probing on every refresh. This requires no TokenStorage interface changes and fixes the problem for all storage backends without requiring them to opt in, while also closing a potential AS-confusion gap that #2492 doesn't address.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs trace back to the same gap: _initialize() doesn't recompute token_expiry_time when it loads a stored OAuthToken. #1784 fixes this at the source with a 4-line change in _initialize() (calling context.update_token_expiry when expires_in is present) plus a dedicated expired_tokens fixture/test. #2875's own inline comment states the identical root cause ('A provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time, so is_token_valid() treats the stale token as valid... the proactive-refresh branch above is skipped') but instead of restoring the field, it adds a larger workaround inside the 401-handling branch of async_auth_flow that tries the stored refresh_token before falling back to full re-authorization. That workaround only runs after a request has already failed with an expired token, whereas fixing _initialize() directly restores proactive refresh and prevents the unnecessary failed request in the first place, making #2875's added branch redundant once applied.

members.author: Dharit13

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs target the missing oauth_metadata on cold start, but via different mechanisms. #2492 adds get_oauth_metadata/set_oauth_metadata to the TokenStorage protocol and persists metadata externally, but the new methods default to no-ops in the base class, so the refresh-after-restart bug remains unfixed for any existing TokenStorage implementation that isn't updated to actually persist metadata. #3263 fixes the same gap unconditionally on the client side by re-running AS discovery before a cold-start refresh whenever oauth_metadata is missing, and additionally adds an issuer-binding check plus an eager_discovery_attempted flag to avoid re-probing on every refresh. This requires no TokenStorage interface changes and fixes the problem for all storage backends without requiring them to opt in, while also closing a potential AS-confusion gap that #2492 doesn't address.

clusters.pick_reason: #2962's fix is grounded in a specific spec citation (SEP-1577) and a linked issue (#2960) demonstrating that raising here is a spec-compliance bug, not just a bad message — a tool_use is not required to be followed by a tool_result. #3053's diff assumes the opposite: that raising in this case is correct and only the wording needs improving, which reintroduces the exact false-positive #2962 fixes. members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs edit the exact same conditional in validate_tool_use_result_messages (src/mcp/server/validation.py) that governs what happens when a preceding assistant message contains tool_use blocks with no corresponding tool_result blocks in the next message. They reach opposite conclusions about the correct behavior for that same case: #2962 makes validation skip the ID-matching check entirely when there are no tool_result blocks at all (has_tool_results guard), so no error is raised — citing SEP-1577's requirement that tool_result must be preceded by tool_use, but not the reverse. #3053 keeps the error path for that exact case but replaces the confusing 'ids ... do not match' message with a new explicit raise ('tool_use blocks must be followed by matching tool_result blocks') — i.e. it still raises where #2962 stops raising. clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs trace back to the same gap: _initialize() doesn't recompute token_expiry_time when it loads a stored OAuthToken. #1784 fixes this at the source with a 4-line change in _initialize() (calling context.update_token_expiry when expires_in is present) plus a dedicated expired_tokens fixture/test. #2875's own inline comment states the identical root cause ('A provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time, so is_token_valid() treats the stale token as valid... the proactive-refresh branch above is skipped') but instead of restoring the field, it adds a larger workaround inside the 401-handling branch of async_auth_flow that tries the stored refresh_token before falling back to full re-authorization. That workaround only runs after a request has already failed with an expired token, whereas fixing _initialize() directly restores proactive refresh and prevents the unnecessary failed request in the first place, making #2875's added branch redundant once applied.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs target the missing oauth_metadata on cold start, but via different mechanisms. #2492 adds get_oauth_metadata/set_oauth_metadata to the TokenStorage protocol and persists metadata externally, but the new methods default to no-ops in the base class, so the refresh-after-restart bug remains unfixed for any existing TokenStorage implementation that isn't updated to actually persist metadata. #3263 fixes the same gap unconditionally on the client side by re-running AS discovery before a cold-start refresh whenever oauth_metadata is missing, and additionally adds an issuer-binding check plus an eager_discovery_attempted flag to avoid re-probing on every refresh. This requires no TokenStorage interface changes and fixes the problem for all storage backends without requiring them to opt in, while also closing a potential AS-confusion gap that #2492 doesn't address.

clusters.pick_reason: #2962's fix is grounded in a specific spec citation (SEP-1577) and a linked issue (#2960) demonstrating that raising here is a spec-compliance bug, not just a bad message — a tool_use is not required to be followed by a tool_result. #3053's diff assumes the opposite: that raising in this case is correct and only the wording needs improving, which reintroduces the exact false-positive #2962 fixes. members.title: fix(auth): match complete WWW-Authenticate parameters
members.author: tarunag10
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: WWW-Authenticate header parsing used naive substring/regex matching to find auth-param values (e.g. resource_metadata, error, error_description), which could false-positive match text that only appears as a substring elsewhere in the header (including inside quoted values) instead of matching a true, complete auth-param. Both PRs replace this with a quote-aware, comma-delimited tokenizer for the header. (2 PRs)

members.cluster_pick_reason: Both add a quote/escape-aware comma splitter for WWW-Authenticate in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py, but #3012's diff is the more complete and minimal fix: it deletes the now-dead `import re`, showing the old regex-based substring matcher is fully replaced by a single `_iter_www_auth_params` helper feeding directly into `extract_field_from_www_auth`. #3041 instead introduces two cooperating helpers (`_split_www_authenticate_segments` + `_extract_bearer_auth_params`) that add roughly double the net new lines (~82 vs ~39) for the same fix, and its Bearer-scheme-detection loop is cut off before completing its stop condition in the diff, making its full correctness harder to verify. #3012 also keeps the change scoped to fixing the exact substring-match bug without adding scheme-disambiguation logic that isn't exercised by the single-challenge case this codebase actually handles.
